questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an endogenic process?
questions.explanation: Faulting is an endogenic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an exogenic process?
questions.explanation: Coastal erosion is an exogenic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a constructive process?

options.D: Glacial valley deepened by ice erosion

questions.explanation: A delta built by river deposition is an example of a constructive process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a destructive process?

options.B: Alluvial fan built by sediment deposition

questions.explanation: Slope failure through landsliding is an example of a destructive process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can a constructive process be harmful to people?

options.A: No, constructive processes are always beneficial
options.B: Yes, a volcanic eruption can build new land but also destroy settlements
options.C: No, constructive processes never affect people
options.D: Yes, but only in coastal areas

questions.explanation: A volcanic eruption can build new land but also destroy settlements. Geomorphic labels describe landform effects, not whether an event is socially beneficial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What do tectonic processes include?

options.C: Plate divergence, convergence, transform motion, folding, faulting, uplift, subsidence, earthquakes and tectonically related mountain building

questions.explanation: Tectonic processes include plate divergence, convergence, transform motion, folding, faulting, uplift, subsidence, earthquakes and tectonically related mountain building.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does plate tectonics explain?

options.A: Much of the distribution of earthquakes, volcanoes, ocean basins and mountain belts
options.D: Only the distribution of ocean basins

questions.explanation: Plate interactions explain much of the distribution of earthquakes, volcanoes, ocean basins and mountain belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The lithosphere is broken into:
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is broken into tectonic plates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Over which layer do tectonic plates move?
questions.explanation: Tectonic plates move over the more deformable asthenosphere.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What can form at mid-ocean ridges?
questions.explanation: New oceanic crust can form at mid-ocean ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What can oceanic-continental convergence produce?

options.D: A deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain on the overriding continent

questions.explanation: Oceanic-continental convergence can produce a deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain on the overriding continent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What can oceanic-oceanic convergence produce?

options.A: A trench and a volcanic island arc

questions.explanation: Oceanic-oceanic convergence can produce a trench and a volcanic island arc.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What can continental-continental collision produce?

options.C: High mountain belts through compression, folding, faulting and crustal thickening

questions.explanation: Continental-continental collision produces high mountain belts through compression, folding, faulting and crustal thickening.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why can earthquakes occur at transform boundaries?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes can occur at transform boundaries when friction prevents smooth movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to magma at a mid-ocean ridge during seafloor spreading?
questions.explanation: At a mid-ocean ridge, magma rises, cools and solidifies, forming new oceanic lithosphere.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does modern plate tectonics provide?

options.A: The broader mechanism explaining continental movement
options.C: A replacement for continental drift theory

questions.explanation: Modern plate tectonics provides the broader mechanism explaining continental movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: During which eras was Pangaea assembled?

options.A: Late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras

questions.explanation: Pangaea was a supercontinent in which most of Earth's present-day continental landmasses were joined during the late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras before breaking apart.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT evidence supporting continental drift and plate tectonics?

options.A: The jigsaw-like fit of continental margins
options.B: Matching fossils and rock belts across now-separated continents
options.C: The pattern of seafloor magnetic stripes
options.D: The uniform distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes

questions.explanation: The global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes supports plate tectonics, but this distribution is not uniform; it is concentrated along plate boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does isostasy describe?

options.A: The gravitational balance in which the lithosphere floats at an elevation related to its thickness and density
options.B: The formation of new oceanic crust
options.C: The movement of plates past each other
options.D: The eruption of magma onto the surface

questions.explanation: Isostasy is the gravitational balance in which the lithosphere floats at an elevation related to its thickness and density over the more deformable mantle.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What happens to land after a heavy load such as a large ice sheet is removed?
questions.explanation: Isostatic rebound is the gradual uplift of land after a heavy load, such as a large ice sheet, is removed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are described as:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are collision-related fold mountains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andes are associated with:
questions.explanation: The Andes are associated with oceanic-continental convergence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is required for a new ocean basin to form?

options.A: Continental rifting followed by seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Continental rifting can thin and split a continent. Continued extension may allow seafloor spreading to begin, producing a new ocean basin with a mid-ocean ridge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are plate boundaries always single narrow lines?

options.B: No, they are zones of interaction and deformation may be distributed across broad regions

questions.explanation: Plate boundaries are zones of interaction, not always single narrow lines. Their deformation may be distributed across broad regions, and real plate-boundary systems can be complex.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Tectonic uplift in the Himalayas:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are a young fold mountain system associated with collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates; tectonic uplift continues.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: During which geological interval did the Deccan Traps form?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps formed by large-scale volcanic eruptions in the Late Cretaceous to early Paleogene interval.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain is located:

options.B: In a foreland basin south of the Himalayas
options.D: East of the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain is an extensive alluvial plain built largely by river deposition in a foreland basin south of the Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Western Ghats are a major escarpment along:

options.A: The eastern side of peninsular India
options.B: The western side of peninsular India
options.C: The northern side of peninsular India
options.D: The southern side of peninsular India

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are a major escarpment along the western side of peninsular India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar region is associated with:

options.A: The India-Burma plate interaction and subduction system

questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar region is part of an active tectonic and island-arc setting associated with the India-Burma plate interaction and subduction system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about exogenic processes is correct?

options.C: Exogenic processes do not only destroy relief; deposition creates new landforms
options.D: Exogenic processes only occur on continents

questions.explanation: Exogenic processes do not only destroy relief; deposition creates new landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the asthenosphere is correct?

options.A: It is a continuous layer of liquid magma
options.B: It is predominantly solid but ductile over long timescales

questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is predominantly solid but ductile over long timescales; it is not a continuous layer of liquid magma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At transform boundaries, plates:
questions.explanation: At transform boundaries, plates slide past.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An anticline is generally ______ and a syncline is generally ______.
questions.explanation: An anticline is generally arch-shaped and a syncline trough-shaped.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Geomorphology = scientific study of:

options.A: Landforms and the processes shaping them

questions.explanation: Geomorphology = scientific study of landforms and the processes shaping them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Internal heat and gravity are major drivers of:
questions.explanation: Internal heat and gravity are major drivers of endogenic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Solar energy and gravity are major drivers of:
questions.explanation: Solar energy and gravity are major drivers of exogenic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Lithosphere =
questions.explanation: Lithosphere = crust plus rigid uppermost mantle.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The three main plate-boundary types are:
questions.explanation: Three main plate-boundary types: divergent, convergent and transform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction commonly occurs at:
questions.explanation: Subduction commonly occurs at convergent boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are associated with:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are associated with continental collision.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: A mountain is a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface and is an example of a landform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a landform?
questions.explanation: A highway is a man-made feature, not a natural landform. Plateaus, valleys and dunes are natural landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is studied under geomorphology?

options.A: The development of landforms through geological time
options.C: The materials of which landforms are made

questions.explanation: Geomorphology studies the form and shape of landforms, the materials of which they are made, the processes that create and modify them, their spatial distribution, and their development through geological time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Geomorphology is a specialised field at the intersection of which two disciplines?
questions.explanation: Geomorphology is a specialised field at the intersection of geology and physical geography, focusing on landforms and the processes responsible for them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a specialised field of geomorphology?
questions.explanation: Fluvial, glacial and coastal geomorphology are all specialised fields of geomorphology.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a specialised field of geomorphology?
questions.explanation: Aeolian, karst and volcanic geomorphology are all specialised fields of geomorphology.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a specialised field of geomorphology?
questions.explanation: Tectonic, hillslope and planetary geomorphology are all specialised fields of geomorphology.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Geomorphology helps in:

options.A: Assessing landslide, flood, coastal-erosion and earthquake-related hazards

questions.explanation: Geomorphology helps explain natural landscapes; assess landslide, flood, coastal-erosion and earthquake-related hazards; guide infrastructure and land-use planning; understand soil and sediment development; manage watersheds; and interpret environmental change.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What do internal forces do to the Earth's crust?

options.B: They deform, uplift, fracture or lower parts of the Earth's crust
options.D: They have no effect on the crust

questions.explanation: Internal forces deform, uplift, fracture or lower parts of the Earth's crust and are commonly called endogenic forces.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Earthquakes are:

options.B: Sudden releases of accumulated strain closely associated with tectonic activity

questions.explanation: Earthquakes are sudden releases of accumulated strain and are closely associated with tectonic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Orogeny usually involves:

options.A: Plate convergence, compression, folding, faulting, crustal thickening and sometimes magmatism

questions.explanation: Orogeny is the process of mountain building, usually involving plate convergence, compression, folding, faulting, crustal thickening and sometimes magmatism.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Epeirogeny can produce:
questions.explanation: Epeirogeny can alter relative sea level and produce raised or submerged coastal features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of fault forms mainly under extension?
questions.explanation: A normal fault forms mainly under extension when the hanging wall moves down relative to the footwall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of fault forms under compression?
questions.explanation: A reverse fault forms under compression when the hanging wall moves up.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A thrust fault is a:
questions.explanation: A thrust fault is a low-angle reverse fault.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A strike-slip fault involves mainly:
questions.explanation: A strike-slip fault involves mainly horizontal movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A rift valley is commonly formed under:
questions.explanation: A rift valley is an elongated depression formed when a block of crust subsides between approximately parallel faults, commonly under extensional tectonic forces.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Volcanism involves the movement of:

options.B: Magma and associated gases from the Earth's interior into or towards the crust and surface

questions.explanation: Volcanism is the movement of magma and associated gases from the Earth's interior into or towards the crust and surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a volcanic landform?
questions.explanation: A caldera is a volcanic landform. Moraines, cirques and drumlins are glacial landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a volcanic landform?
questions.explanation: A lava dome is a volcanic landform. Arêtes, horns and U-shaped valleys are glacial landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The epicentre is located:

options.B: Directly above the focus on the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Running water is an exogenic agent. Magma, mantle convection and radioactive decay are related to internal processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Glaciers are an exogenic agent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Wind is an exogenic agent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Sea waves and currents are exogenic agents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Temperature changes are an exogenic agent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic agent?
questions.explanation: Living organisms are exogenic agents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Physical weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces without:
questions.explanation: Physical or mechanical weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces without substantially changing its mineral composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chemical weathering alters minerals through:
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering alters minerals through reactions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Biological weathering results from:

options.A: The activity of organisms and may be physical or chemical

questions.explanation: Biological weathering results from the activity of organisms, and may be physical or chemical.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Erosion involves:

options.A: Only the breakdown of rock in place

questions.explanation: Erosion involves the wearing away and removal of rock or soil. Unlike weathering, erosion involves removal and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Transportation in geomorphology is the movement of:

options.B: Weathered or eroded material by water, wind, ice, waves or gravity

questions.explanation: Transportation is the movement of weathered or eroded material by water, wind, ice, waves or gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a way rivers carry sediment?
questions.explanation: Rivers may carry sediment in solution, suspension, saltation and traction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Deposition occurs when:

options.B: A transporting agent loses energy or capacity and lays down the sediment it carries
options.C: Rock is broken down in place

questions.explanation: Deposition occurs when a transporting agent loses energy or capacity and lays down the sediment it carries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mass wasting is driven by:
questions.explanation: Mass wasting is the downslope movement of soil, rock or debris under gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of mass wasting?
questions.explanation: A landslide is an example of mass wasting. Deltas, dunes and cirques are landforms formed by other processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Solar energy drives:

options.A: The water cycle, winds and many temperature-related processes

questions.explanation: Solar energy drives the water cycle, winds and many temperature-related processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Gravity helps in:

options.A: Moving water downhill and driving mass movement

questions.explanation: Gravity moves water downhill, drives mass movement and helps transport sediment from higher to lower elevations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A V-shaped valley is formed by running water. Cirques, moraines and drumlins are glacial landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A gorge is formed by running water. Arêtes, horns and U-shaped valleys are glacial landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A waterfall is formed by running water. Calderas, craters and lava domes are volcanic landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A floodplain is formed by running water. Sinkholes, caves and stalactites are formed by groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A meander is formed by running water. Yardangs, mushroom rocks and dunes are formed by wind.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A levee is formed by running water. Cliffs, wave-cut platforms and stacks are formed by sea waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by running water?
questions.explanation: A delta is formed by running water. Talus slopes, rockfalls and landslides are formed by gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by groundwater?
questions.explanation: A cave is formed by groundwater. Cirques and moraines are glacial; dunes are aeolian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by groundwater?
questions.explanation: A sinkhole is formed by groundwater. Arêtes and horns are glacial; yardangs are aeolian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by groundwater?
questions.explanation: A stalactite is formed by groundwater. Drumlins are glacial; mushroom rocks are aeolian; beaches are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by groundwater?
questions.explanation: A stalagmite is formed by groundwater. U-shaped valleys are glacial; loess is aeolian; spits are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by groundwater?
questions.explanation: Karst landscapes are formed by groundwater dissolving soluble rocks. Cirques are glacial, dunes are aeolian, and cliffs are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: A cirque is formed by glaciers. Deltas and meanders are fluvial; dunes are aeolian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: An arête is formed by glaciers. Floodplains are fluvial; yardangs are aeolian; beaches are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: A horn is formed by glaciers. Levees are fluvial; mushroom rocks are aeolian; spits are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: A U-shaped valley is formed by glaciers. V-shaped valleys, gorges and waterfalls are formed by running water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: A moraine is formed by glaciers. Sinkholes, caves and stalactites are formed by groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by glaciers?
questions.explanation: A drumlin is formed by glaciers. Deltas are fluvial; dunes are aeolian; cliffs are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by wind?
questions.explanation: A deflation hollow is formed by wind. Cirques and moraines are glacial; meanders are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by wind?
questions.explanation: A yardang is formed by wind. Arêtes are glacial; floodplains are fluvial; beaches are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by wind?
questions.explanation: A mushroom rock is formed by wind. Horns are glacial; levees are fluvial; spits are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by wind?
questions.explanation: A dune is formed by wind. Caves, sinkholes and stalagmites are formed by groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by wind?
questions.explanation: Loess is formed by wind. Deltas and meanders are fluvial; cliffs are coastal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A cliff is formed by sea waves. Cirques and moraines are glacial; dunes are aeolian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A wave-cut platform is formed by sea waves. Arêtes are glacial; yardangs are aeolian; floodplains are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A sea cave is formed by sea waves. Horns are glacial; dunes are aeolian; meanders are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A sea arch is formed by sea waves. Drumlins are glacial; loess is aeolian; levees are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A sea stack is formed by sea waves. Sinkholes, caves and stalactites are formed by groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A beach is formed by sea waves. Cirques and moraines are glacial; dunes are aeolian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by sea waves?
questions.explanation: A spit is formed by sea waves. Arêtes are glacial; yardangs are aeolian; floodplains are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform formed by gravity?
questions.explanation: A talus slope is formed by gravity-driven mass movement. Cirques are glacial; dunes are aeolian; deltas are fluvial.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Rivers erode:
questions.explanation: Rivers erode vertically and laterally, transport sediment and deposit it where velocity or carrying capacity decreases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Upper courses of rivers commonly show:
questions.explanation: Upper courses commonly show valleys and rapids.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Middle courses of rivers often develop:
questions.explanation: Middle courses often develop meanders.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Lower courses of rivers commonly develop:

options.B: Floodplains, levees and deltas or estuaries

questions.explanation: Lower courses commonly develop floodplains, levees and deltas or estuaries depending on coastal conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Glaciers erode by:
questions.explanation: Moving ice erodes by abrasion and plucking and deposits unsorted sediment called till.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Glaciers deposit:
questions.explanation: Glaciers deposit unsorted sediment called till.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wind removes loose particles by:
questions.explanation: Wind removes loose particles by deflation, wears surfaces by abrasion and deposits sediment when wind energy declines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wind wears surfaces by:
questions.explanation: Wind wears surfaces by abrasion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Waves erode through:
questions.explanation: Waves erode through hydraulic action and abrasion, move sediment along coasts by longshore drift, and deposit it to form beaches, spits and bars.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Waves deposit sediment to form:
questions.explanation: Waves deposit sediment to form beaches, spits and bars.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which forces often build relief or create structural features?
questions.explanation: Endogenic forces often build relief or create structural features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which forces often wear down, redistribute or reshape relief?
questions.explanation: Exogenic forces often wear down, redistribute or reshape relief.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can endogenic processes create depressions and destructive hazards?

options.B: Yes, endogenic processes can create depressions and destructive hazards

questions.explanation: Endogenic processes can create depressions and destructive hazards, while exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can exogenic processes build landforms through deposition?

options.B: Yes, exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition such as deltas, beaches and dunes
options.C: No, only endogenic processes build landforms
options.D: Yes, but only through volcanic activity

questions.explanation: Exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition, such as deltas, beaches and dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The landscape is the combined outcome of:
questions.explanation: The landscape is the combined outcome of interacting endogenic and exogenic processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Tectonic uplift is a constructive force. Weathering, river erosion and wave erosion are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Volcanic accumulation is a constructive force. Glacial erosion, wind abrasion and landslides are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Lava flows are a constructive force. Weathering, river erosion and wave erosion are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Sediment deposition by rivers is a constructive force. Glacial erosion, wind abrasion and landslides are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Dune formation is a constructive force. Weathering, river erosion and wave erosion are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: The growth of coral reefs is a constructive force. Glacial erosion, wind abrasion and landslides are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: Weathering is a destructive force. Tectonic uplift, volcanic accumulation and sediment deposition are constructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: River erosion is a destructive force. Lava flows, dune formation and coral reef growth are constructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: Glacial erosion is a destructive force. Tectonic uplift, volcanic accumulation and sediment deposition are constructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: Wave erosion is a destructive force. Lava flows, dune formation and coral reef growth are constructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: Wind abrasion is a destructive force. Tectonic uplift, volcanic accumulation and sediment deposition are constructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a destructive force?
questions.explanation: Landslides are a destructive force. Lava flows, dune formation and coral reef growth are constructive.

options.A: Earthquakes, volcanoes, ocean basins and mountain belts

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The asthenosphere is located:
questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is a relatively weak, ductile part of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a divergent boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, two plates move apart.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a divergent boundary, mantle material rises and partially melts because:
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, mantle material rises and partially melts as pressure decreases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: New oceanic crust forms at:
questions.explanation: New oceanic crust can form at mid-ocean ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Continental extension can produce:

options.B: Rift valleys and eventually a new ocean basin

questions.explanation: On continents, extension can produce rift valleys and eventually a new ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a convergent boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a convergent boundary, two plates move towards each other.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At an oceanic-continental convergent boundary, the denser oceanic lithosphere:
questions.explanation: The denser oceanic lithosphere commonly subducts beneath the continental plate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An oceanic-continental convergent boundary can produce:

options.D: A deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain

questions.explanation: An oceanic-continental convergent boundary can produce a deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain on the overriding continent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At an oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary, one oceanic plate:
questions.explanation: At an oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary, one oceanic plate commonly subducts beneath the other.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary can produce:

options.A: A trench and a volcanic island arc

questions.explanation: An oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary can produce a trench and a volcanic island arc.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a continental-continental convergent boundary, neither plate readily sinks deeply because:
questions.explanation: Neither plate readily sinks deeply because continental crust is relatively buoyant.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a continental-continental convergent boundary, the crust is:
questions.explanation: The crust is compressed, folded, faulted and thickened, producing high mountain belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a transform boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a transform boundary, two plates slide laterally past one another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Crust is generally neither created nor destroyed at:
questions.explanation: Crust is generally neither created nor destroyed at transform boundaries, although earthquakes can occur when friction prevents smooth movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction usually occurs at:
questions.explanation: Subduction is the process in which one lithospheric plate descends beneath another into the mantle, usually at a convergent boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction is commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: Subduction is commonly associated with trenches, earthquakes and volcanic arcs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Seafloor spreading is the formation of new oceanic lithosphere at:
questions.explanation: Seafloor spreading is the formation of new oceanic lithosphere at a divergent boundary, especially along a mid-ocean ridge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Alfred Wegener proposed the idea of:
questions.explanation: Continental drift is the idea, proposed by Alfred Wegener, that continents were once joined and have moved apart.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pangaea was:
questions.explanation: Pangaea was a supercontinent in which most of Earth's present-day continental landmasses were joined.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following supports continental drift?

options.A: The jigsaw-like fit of continental margins
options.C: Palaeoclimatic evidence such as glacial deposits

questions.explanation: The jigsaw-like fit of continental margins, matching fossils and rock belts, palaeoclimatic evidence, seafloor magnetic stripes, ocean-floor age patterns, and the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes support continental drift and plate tectonics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following supports plate tectonics?

options.A: The pattern of seafloor magnetic stripes
options.C: The global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes

questions.explanation: The pattern of seafloor magnetic stripes, ocean-floor age patterns, and the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes support plate tectonics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Isostasy involves the lithosphere floating at an elevation related to its:
questions.explanation: Isostasy is the gravitational balance in which the lithosphere floats at an elevation related to its thickness and density over the more deformable mantle.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following can cause vertical adjustment in isostasy?
questions.explanation: Changes such as erosion, sediment loading or melting of ice can cause vertical adjustment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Post-glacial rebound is occurring in:

options.B: Parts of Africa and South America

questions.explanation: Parts of Scandinavia and Canada are experiencing post-glacial rebound.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mountains can form through:
questions.explanation: Mountains can form through continental collision and crustal thickening, subduction-related volcanism, fault-block uplift or volcanic accumulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are an example of:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are collision-related fold mountains.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andes are an example of mountains associated with:
questions.explanation: The Andes are associated with oceanic-continental convergence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A new ocean basin can form through:

options.A: Continental rifting followed by seafloor spreading

questions.explanation: Continental rifting can thin and split a continent. Continued extension may allow seafloor spreading to begin, producing a new ocean basin with a mid-ocean ridge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Plate boundaries are:

options.B: Zones of interaction whose deformation may be distributed across broad regions

questions.explanation: Plate boundaries are zones of interaction, not always single narrow lines. Their deformation may be distributed across broad regions, and real plate-boundary systems can be complex.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are:

options.B: A young fold mountain system with continuing tectonic uplift

questions.explanation: The Himalayas are a young fold mountain system associated with collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates; tectonic uplift continues.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Deccan Traps are an example of:
questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps are an extensive basaltic lava province formed by large-scale volcanic eruptions; they are an example of flood-basalt volcanism.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Narmada and Tapi valleys are:
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapi valleys are often described in Indian geography as rift-related or fault-controlled valleys; their structural history is complex.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain is:

options.B: An extensive alluvial plain built largely by river deposition in a foreland basin south of the Himalayas

questions.explanation: The Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain is an extensive alluvial plain built largely by river deposition in a foreland basin south of the Himalayas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Western Ghats are:

options.A: A major escarpment along the western side of peninsular India

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are a major escarpment along the western side of peninsular India, shaped by long-term tectonic, erosional and denudational processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar region is associated with:

options.A: The India-Burma plate interaction and subduction system

questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar region is part of an active tectonic and island-arc setting associated with the India-Burma plate interaction and subduction system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Geomorphology is not merely the study of mountains; it studies:

options.B: All landforms and the processes shaping them

questions.explanation: Geomorphology is not merely the study of mountains; it studies all landforms and the processes shaping them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Endogenic means:

options.A: Originating at or near the surface

questions.explanation: Endogenic means originating within the Earth; exogenic means operating at or near the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Exogenic means:

options.B: Operating at or near the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: Exogenic means operating at or near the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Weathering does not itself require:
questions.explanation: Weathering does not itself require transportation; erosion involves removal and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Deposition is a constructive process even though it is driven by:
questions.explanation: Deposition is a constructive process even though it is driven by an external agent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Endogenic does not mean only mountain building; it also includes:
questions.explanation: Endogenic does not mean only mountain building; it also includes subsidence, faulting, earthquakes and volcanism.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Exogenic processes do not only destroy relief; deposition creates:
questions.explanation: Exogenic processes do not only destroy relief; deposition creates new landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The asthenosphere is predominantly solid but ductile over long timescales; it is not:

options.A: A continuous layer of liquid magma

questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is predominantly solid but ductile over long timescales; it is not a continuous layer of liquid magma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At divergent boundaries plates move apart; at convergent boundaries they move together; at transform boundaries they:
questions.explanation: At divergent boundaries plates move apart; at convergent boundaries they move together; at transform boundaries they slide past.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are collision-related mountains, whereas the Andes are strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are collision-related mountains, whereas the Andes are strongly associated with oceanic-continental subduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The earthquake focus is inside Earth; the epicentre is:
questions.explanation: The earthquake focus is inside Earth; the epicentre is on the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An anticline is generally arch-shaped and a syncline trough-shaped; erosion can alter:
questions.explanation: An anticline is generally arch-shaped and a syncline trough-shaped; do not confuse these with a hill and valley in every real-world case because erosion can alter surface appearance.

questions.question: Greek roots of geomorphology are:

options.B: geo = water; morphe = rock; logos = science
options.C: geo = air; morphe = shape; logos = theory
options.D: geo = land; morphe = structure; logos = analysis

questions.explanation: Greek roots: geo = Earth; morphe = form; logos = study.

questions.question: Weathering breaks down rock in place; erosion:
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down rock in place; erosion removes and transports it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Deposition builds features such as:
questions.explanation: Deposition builds features such as deltas, beaches and dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mass wasting is downslope movement under:
questions.explanation: Mass wasting is downslope movement under gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Magma is underground molten rock; lava is:
questions.explanation: Magma is underground molten rock; lava is erupted magma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Focus is the earthquake origin; epicentre lies directly above it at the:
questions.explanation: Focus is the earthquake origin; epicentre lies directly above it at the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Lithosphere = crust plus:
questions.explanation: Lithosphere = crust plus rigid uppermost mantle.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Three main plate-boundary types are:
questions.explanation: Three main plate-boundary types: divergent, convergent and transform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mid-ocean ridges are associated with:
questions.explanation: Mid-ocean ridges are associated with seafloor spreading.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction commonly occurs at:
questions.explanation: Subduction commonly occurs at convergent boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are associated with:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are associated with continental collision.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The San Andreas Fault system is a classic example of:

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Geomorphology is primarily the scientific study of:

options.B: Landforms and the processes shaping them

questions.explanation: Geomorphology is primarily the scientific study of landforms and the processes shaping them.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Endogenic forces originate:
questions.explanation: Endogenic forces originate within the Earth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an exogenic process?
questions.explanation: Weathering is an exogenic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The broad process of mountain building is called:
questions.explanation: Orogeny is the broad process of mountain building.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A down-dropped block between faults is a:
questions.explanation: A graben is a down-dropped block between faults.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The point inside Earth where an earthquake begins is the:
questions.explanation: The focus is the point inside Earth where an earthquake begins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process adds sediment to build a delta?
questions.explanation: Deposition adds sediment to build a delta.

questions.question: At a divergent plate boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a divergent plate boundary, plates move apart.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Himalayas are mainly associated with:
questions.explanation: The Himalayas are mainly associated with continental collision.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The San Andreas Fault system is associated with a:
questions.explanation: The San Andreas Fault system is associated with a transform boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about weathering is correct?

options.B: It breaks down or alters rock in place

questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down or alters rock in place.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.D: Epicentre—point inside Earth where rupture begins

questions.explanation: Horst is a relatively uplifted fault block.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following best defines the scope of geomorphology?

options.B: The study of landforms, their origin, evolution, distribution and the processes that shape the Earth's surface
options.C: The study of ocean salinity only
options.D: The study of atmospheric pressure only

questions.explanation: Geomorphology is the scientific study of landforms, their origin, evolution, distribution and the processes that shape the Earth's surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly differentiates endogenic and exogenic forces?

options.A: Endogenic forces operate at the surface; exogenic forces originate within Earth
options.B: Endogenic forces originate within Earth; exogenic forces operate at or near the surface
options.D: Both operate only at the surface

questions.explanation: Endogenic forces originate within Earth; exogenic forces operate at or near the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the relationship between weathering, erosion, transportation and deposition?
questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down rock in place, erosion removes and transports material, transportation moves it, and deposition lays it down.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes orogeny from epeirogeny?

options.A: Orogeny is broad regional uplift; epeirogeny is mountain building
options.B: Orogeny is mountain building; epeirogeny is broad regional uplift or subsidence
options.D: Both are broad regional uplift processes

questions.explanation: Orogeny is mountain building; epeirogeny is broad regional uplift or subsidence.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the three major types of plate boundaries?

options.A: Divergent (plates move apart), convergent (plates move towards each other) and transform (plates slide past)
options.B: Divergent (plates move towards each other), convergent (plates move apart) and transform (plates slide past)
options.C: Divergent (plates slide past), convergent (plates move apart) and transform (plates move towards each other)
options.D: Divergent (plates stop), convergent (plates move apart) and transform (plates move towards each other)

questions.explanation: Divergent boundaries: plates move apart; convergent boundaries: plates move towards each other; transform boundaries: plates slide past.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do constructive and destructive processes jointly shape landscapes?

options.A: Constructive processes build or add material while destructive processes wear down or remove material; both act together to shape landscapes
options.B: Constructive processes only destroy and destructive processes only build

questions.explanation: Constructive processes build or add material while destructive processes wear down or remove material; both act together to shape landscapes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a specialised field of geomorphology?
questions.explanation: The specialised fields include fluvial, glacial, coastal, aeolian, karst, volcanic, tectonic, hillslope and planetary geomorphology. Astrological geomorphology is not a recognised field.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which branch of geomorphology studies volcanic features?
questions.explanation: Volcanic geomorphology studies volcanic features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which branch of geomorphology studies tectonic landforms?
questions.explanation: Tectonic geomorphology studies tectonic landforms.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which branch of geomorphology studies hillslopes?
questions.explanation: Hillslope geomorphology studies hillslopes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following contributes to mantle convection and the movement of lithospheric plates?

options.B: Residual heat from Earth's formation, heat from radioactive decay and gravitational energy

questions.explanation: Residual heat from Earth's formation, heat produced by radioactive decay, and gravitational energy contribute to mantle convection and the movement of lithospheric plates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is produced by diastrophism?

options.A: Folds, faults, mountains, plateaus, basins and rift valleys

questions.explanation: Diastrophism produces features such as folds, faults, mountains, plateaus, basins and rift valleys.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Orogenic movements are mainly associated with:

options.A: Broad vertical uplift of large regions

questions.explanation: Orogenic movements are mainly associated with mountain building and intense deformation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Epeirogenic movements involve:

options.B: Broad, generally vertical uplift or subsidence of large crustal regions

questions.explanation: Epeirogenic movements involve broad, generally vertical uplift or subsidence of large crustal regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What can epeirogeny alter?

options.A: Relative sea level and produce raised or submerged coastal features

questions.explanation: Epeirogeny can alter relative sea level and produce raised or submerged coastal features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following may be present in real fold structures?

options.C: Overturned, recumbent, asymmetrical or complex structures

questions.explanation: Real structures may be overturned, recumbent, asymmetrical or complex.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a landform created by volcanism?
questions.explanation: Moraines are glacial depositional features, not volcanic landforms. Volcanism creates volcanic cones, lava plateaus, volcanic mountains, calderas, craters, lava domes and volcanic islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does energy released during an earthquake travel?
questions.explanation: The released energy travels as seismic waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Earthquakes also occur in:

options.B: Volcanic regions and, less commonly, through other processes

questions.explanation: Earthquakes also occur in volcanic regions and, less commonly, through other processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: External forces are also called:
questions.explanation: External forces are also called exogenic forces.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Does weathering require the removed material to be transported?

options.B: No, it does not require the removed material to be transported

questions.explanation: Weathering is the breakdown or alteration of rocks in place. It does not require the removed material to be transported.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Physical weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces without substantially changing its:
questions.explanation: Physical or mechanical weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces without substantially changing its mineral composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chemical weathering alters minerals through:
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering alters minerals through reactions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Biological weathering may be:
questions.explanation: Biological weathering results from the activity of organisms, and may be physical or chemical.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Erosion involves:

options.A: Only the breakdown of rock in place

questions.explanation: Erosion involves the wearing away and removal of rock or soil. Unlike weathering, erosion involves removal and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Transportation in geomorphology is the movement of:

options.B: Weathered or eroded material by water, wind, ice, waves or gravity

questions.explanation: Transportation is the movement of weathered or eroded material by water, wind, ice, waves or gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a way rivers carry sediment?

questions.explanation: Glaciers deposit unsorted sediment called till.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wind removes loose particles by:
questions.explanation: Wind removes loose particles by deflation, wears surfaces by abrasion and deposits sediment when wind energy declines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wind wears surfaces by:
questions.explanation: Wind wears surfaces by abrasion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Wind deposits sediment when:
questions.explanation: Wind deposits sediment when wind energy declines.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Waves erode through:
questions.explanation: Waves erode through hydraulic action and abrasion, move sediment along coasts by longshore drift, and deposit it to form beaches, spits and bars.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Waves deposit sediment to form:
questions.explanation: Waves deposit sediment to form beaches, spits and bars.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is longshore drift?

options.A: The movement of sediment along coasts by wave action
options.B: The downslope movement of soil under gravity
options.D: The deposition of loess by wind

questions.explanation: Waves move sediment along coasts by longshore drift.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What factors influence the shape and rate of coastal change?
questions.explanation: Resistant rock and local geology influence the shape and rate of coastal change.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which forces often build relief or create structural features?
questions.explanation: Endogenic forces often build relief or create structural features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which forces often wear down, redistribute or reshape relief?
questions.explanation: Exogenic forces often wear down, redistribute or reshape relief.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of an endogenic process?
questions.explanation: Himalayan mountain building is an example of an endogenic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of an exogenic process?
questions.explanation: River erosion is an example of an exogenic process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can endogenic processes create depressions and destructive hazards?

options.B: Yes, endogenic processes can create depressions and destructive hazards

questions.explanation: Endogenic processes can create depressions and destructive hazards, while exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can exogenic processes build landforms through deposition?

options.B: Yes, exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition such as deltas, beaches and dunes
options.C: No, only endogenic processes build landforms
options.D: Yes, but only through volcanic activity

questions.explanation: Exogenic processes can build landforms through deposition, such as deltas, beaches and dunes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The landscape is the combined outcome of:
questions.explanation: The landscape is the combined outcome of interacting endogenic and exogenic processes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Tectonic uplift is a constructive force. Weathering, river erosion and wave erosion are destructive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a constructive force?
questions.explanation: Volcanic accumulation is a constructive force. Glacial erosion, wind abrasion and landslides are destructive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Plate interactions explain much of the distribution of:

options.A: Earthquakes, volcanoes, ocean basins and mountain belts

questions.explanation: Plate interactions explain much of the distribution of earthquakes, volcanoes, ocean basins and mountain belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The asthenosphere is:

options.B: Solid rock that can flow slowly over geological time

questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is solid rock that can flow slowly over geological time, not a global ocean of magma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The asthenosphere is located:
questions.explanation: The asthenosphere is a relatively weak, ductile part of the upper mantle beneath the lithosphere.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a divergent boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, two plates move apart.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a divergent boundary, mantle material rises and partially melts because:
questions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, mantle material rises and partially melts as pressure decreases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: New oceanic crust forms at:
questions.explanation: New oceanic crust can form at mid-ocean ridges.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Continental extension can produce:

options.B: Rift valleys and eventually a new ocean basin

questions.explanation: On continents, extension can produce rift valleys and eventually a new ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a convergent boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a convergent boundary, two plates move towards each other.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At an oceanic-continental convergent boundary, the denser oceanic lithosphere:
questions.explanation: The denser oceanic lithosphere commonly subducts beneath the continental plate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An oceanic-continental convergent boundary can produce:

options.D: A deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain

questions.explanation: An oceanic-continental convergent boundary can produce a deep-sea trench, earthquakes and a volcanic mountain chain on the overriding continent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At an oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary, one oceanic plate:
questions.explanation: At an oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary, one oceanic plate commonly subducts beneath the other.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary can produce:

options.A: A trench and a volcanic island arc

questions.explanation: An oceanic-oceanic convergent boundary can produce a trench and a volcanic island arc.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a continental-continental convergent boundary, neither plate readily sinks deeply because:
questions.explanation: Neither plate readily sinks deeply because continental crust is relatively buoyant.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a continental-continental convergent boundary, the crust is:
questions.explanation: The crust is compressed, folded, faulted and thickened, producing high mountain belts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At a transform boundary, plates:
questions.explanation: At a transform boundary, two plates slide laterally past one another.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Crust is generally neither created nor destroyed at:
questions.explanation: Crust is generally neither created nor destroyed at transform boundaries, although earthquakes can occur when friction prevents smooth movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction usually occurs at:
questions.explanation: Subduction is the process in which one lithospheric plate descends beneath another into the mantle, usually at a convergent boundary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Subduction is commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: Subduction is commonly associated with trenches, earthquakes and volcanic arcs.
